review_notes: I read the whole 509-line target file, the relevant definitions in LeanPool/KaltonRoberts/Defs.lean (additiveFunction, distToAdditive, DualCertificate), and searched LeanPool for uses of clm_decompose and clm_indicator'_eq_additiveFunction; clm_decompose has no uses, while clm_indicator'_eq_additiveFunction is used at lines 156 and 163. The findings concern repeated finite-sum reindexing in dual_cert_from_convexHull, repeated epsilon-perturbation machinery in zero_mem_convexHull_of_best_approx, and two proofs of the same standard-basis decomposition. I did not execute Lean; proposed helper statements are sketches and may need binder or instance adjustments (in particular preserving the no-Fintype generality of clm_indicator'_eq_additiveFunction). Excerpts are short single-line or two-line quotations taken verbatim from arXiv source; they are used only for locating the relevant code.

findings.problem: The support decomposition of the finite set c is proved twice. Lines 334–376 reindex the weights w over the positive and negative parts of activeGenerators using sum_subset, sum_union, sum_image and indicator'_injective. Lines 377–450 rebuild the same reindexing for the summand w v • v, and lines 396–414 and 415–435 are nearly copied positive/negative branches that differ only by signs. The certificate conditions therefore depend on two independent proofs of the same finset decomposition.
findings.proposed_change: Extract one decomposition over an arbitrary additive codomain, roughly: for F : (U → ℝ) → β and c : Finset (U → ℝ) with hc : ∀ v ∈ c, v ∈ activeGenerators f M and hM : M ≠ 0, prove ∑ v ∈ c, F v = (∑ S ∈ univ.filter (fun S => f S = M), ∑ v ∈ c, if v = S.indicator' then F v else 0) + (∑ S ∈ univ.filter (fun S => f S = -M), ∑ v ∈ c, if v = -S.indicator' then F v else 0). Proof sketch: each v ∈ c lies in one of the two images by hc; the index S is unique by indicator'_injective; hM makes the positive and negative active sets disjoint; then interchange the finite sums. Instantiate with F := w for the norm-one calculation and F := fun v => w v • v for h_sum_eq, then unfold lam_pos and lam_neg. The hypothesis hc is exactly hw_pos at line 285 and hM comes from hM_pos.
findings.benefit: This states the active-support split once, removes a large duplicated reindexing argument and the mirrored branch proofs, and makes explicit that both certificate conditions use the same disjoint decomposition.

findings.problem: The epsilon perturbation is assembled through separate local proofs h_inactive and h_active, and h_active repeats the same threshold calculation in the f S = M and f S = -M branches. Both displayed thresholds are M divided by the absolute value of additiveFunction a S: in the first branch additiveFunction a S is positive, in the second it is negative. The finite-minimum selection at lines 251–262 is then a third layer of the same construction. This obscures the single real-variable estimate that is actually being used.
findings.proposed_change: Introduce a real helper such as: given hM : 0 < M, hc : |c| = M and hb : 0 < c * b, prove ∃ ε > 0, ∀ ε' ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε, |c - ε' * b| < M (take ε < M / |b| and use that c and b have the same sign), together with additiveFunction (fun i => r * a i) S = r * additiveFunction a S. Then package the whole finite choice as one lemma: from hM : 0 < M, hbound : ∀ S, |f S| ≤ M, and hsign : ∀ S, |f S| = M → 0 < f S * additiveFunction a S, obtain ∃ ε > 0, ∀ S, |f S - additiveFunction (fun i => ε * a i) S| < M, using continuity at ε = 0 in the inactive case and the real helper in the active case, followed by the finite minimum. Call this once in zero_mem_convexHull_of_best_approx, deriving hsign from h_additiveFunction_a_pos and h_additiveFunction_a_neg.
findings.benefit: The Hahn–Banach contradiction no longer contains two copies of the active-case nlinarith threshold proof or two separate epsilon-construction frameworks; the analytic estimate is stated once with its exact hypotheses and can be checked independently.

findings.problem: Both lemmas independently prove the same standard-basis expansion and then apply map_sum. clm_decompose does this for an arbitrary h summed over univ; clm_indicator'_eq_additiveFunction expands S.indicator' as ∑ i ∈ S, Function.update 0 i 1 and repeats the map_sum calculation. clm_decompose has no uses elsewhere in LeanPool, while the specialized lemma is used at lines 156 and 163, so the general proof is currently dead and the specialized proof duplicates it.
findings.proposed_change: Use a single finite-carrier decomposition: for s : Finset U and h supported on s (∀ i, i ∉ s → h i = 0), prove Λ h = ∑ i ∈ s, h i * Λ (Function.update 0 i 1). Proof sketch: h = ∑ i ∈ s, Function.update 0 i (h i) pointwise (Finset.sum_eq_single on s, Finset.sum_eq_zero off s), then apply Λ, map_sum and scalar extraction as in the current clm_decompose. Derive clm_decompose with s := univ, and derive clm_indicator'_eq_additiveFunction with s := S from Finset.indicator', keeping the omit [Fintype U] generality. If no external user of clm_decompose exists, delete it after adding the shared helper.
findings.benefit: There is one proof of the basis decomposition instead of two; the unused general lemma no longer diverges from the specialized one, and the indicator identity follows from the general theorem rather than duplicating its map_sum argument.
